blocks.label: Get To Know Me
blocks.title: From landscape design to land acquisition.
blocks.lede: The through-line is the same in both careers: understanding what a piece of ground will let you do.
paragraphs: {{agent.name}} is a Broker Associate and Partner with The Group Real Estate, recognised for a results-driven approach and deep expertise in the Steamboat Springs and Routt County markets. A Colorado native who relocated from Golden to Steamboat in 2021, she brings an unusual mix of professionalism, precision and patience to every transaction.

Licensed since 2020, she has closed more than 120 transactions totalling over $60 million across Routt and Mesa counties — everything from rural parcels to luxury estates. In 2025 alone she completed 36 transactions and $20 million in sales.

Before real estate, {{agent.first}} built a distinguished twenty-year career as an award-winning landscape designer and horticulturist, earning statewide recognition for transformative projects. She and her husband owned a Denver design-build firm that was featured in national publications and ranked consistently among Colorado's top landscape companies. That foundation gives her clients a rare advantage when evaluating land potential, navigating site development, or envisioning sustainable, environmentally aligned properties across the Yampa Valley.

She also maintains a real estate portfolio of her own — thoughtfully reimagined residences from Denver's Front Range to Palisade — which is the shortest explanation of how she thinks about long-term value.

{{agent.first}} specialises in land acquisition, rural development, investment properties, and South Routt single-family home and ranch sales. With an office in Steamboat and a ranchette near the quiet town of Phippsburg, she stays close to the ranching community she calls home. As a sponsor of the Steamboat Springs Pro Rodeo and a farm producer for the Community Agriculture Alliance, she is genuinely inside the community that defines Routt County.

Clients value her straightforward communication, sharp negotiation and hands-on guidance through the region's complex zoning and permitting processes. Her mission is simple: a real estate experience defined by trust, strategy and results.

Access easements across a neighbour's ground. Whether a slope will ever hold a septic field. Which covenants are enforced and which are decoration.
None of that shows up in an MLS listing, and none of it is answerable from Denver. It is the substance of the work.

blocks.label: Ranch & Land
blocks.title: The questions nobody asks until closing.
blocks.lede: A parcel is a set of permissions, not a picture.
paragraphs: Most land deals in South Routt go sideways for the same handful of reasons, and none of them appear in the listing. Whether there is a legal, recorded, year-round access. Whether the well permit is household-use-only or allows livestock. Whether the buildable envelope survives the setbacks once you account for slope. Whether the county will let you put a second dwelling on it, ever.

{{agent.first}}'s twenty years in landscape design and horticulture were spent answering the physical half of that list — soil, water, drainage, what will grow and what will slide. The regulatory half came with six years of Routt County closings. Buyers get both before they go under contract, not after.

pages.title: Buying in Routt County — Lauren Bloom's Buyer Guide
pages.desc: How Lauren Bloom works with buyers in Steamboat Springs and Routt County: four steps, an honest budget conversation, and the land questions to settle before earnest money.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: Buying here, in four steps.
blocks.lede: Most buyer guides run to ten steps because they are describing paperwork. This one describes decisions — the four that actually change the outcome.

blocks.label: The Four Steps
blocks.title: Four decisions, in order.
blocks.lede: The Group's full buyer process sits behind this — escrow, inspection, appraisal, closing. These are the parts where you and {{agent.first}} do the thinking.

steps.title: Decide your number, not your approval
steps.body: A lender will pre-approve you for more than you want to spend. Set the monthly payment you are comfortable with first, then get pre-qualified against it. In the valley, budget the things a Front Range buyer forgets: plowing, propane, a longer drive to everything, and HOA dues that in some subdivisions carry a water tap.

steps.title: Pick the market before the house
steps.body: Steamboat, Stagecoach, Oak Creek, Phippsburg, Hayden and Clark are six different trade-offs between price, commute, water and covenants. Choosing the wrong one and then hunting for a house inside it is the single most common way buyers waste a season. {{agent.first}} will talk you out of an area if it is wrong for you.

steps.title: Settle the ground questions before earnest money
steps.body: For anything with land attached: recorded year-round access, well permit class, septic feasibility, buildable envelope after setbacks and slope, and whether the county would allow a second dwelling. These are answerable in days and they are the difference between a good parcel and an expensive view.

steps.title: Write an offer that reads as serious
steps.body: Price is one term of several. Inspection window, financing contingency, closing date, post-closing occupancy, what stays with the house. In a thin market the strongest offer is often not the highest one — it is the one the seller believes will actually close.

pages.title: Selling in Routt County — Lauren Bloom's Seller Guide
pages.desc: How Lauren Bloom prices, prepares and markets a Steamboat Springs or Routt County property, and what the first three weeks on market decide.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: Selling here, in four steps.
blocks.lede: One of {{agent.first}}'s clients had a house sit for seven months and two showings with another agent, then took an offer within a month of relisting. Almost all of that difference is made in the first three weeks.

steps.title: Be honest about why you are selling
steps.body: Speed and price are different goals and they need different strategies. Tell {{agent.first}} which one you actually care about — a seller who needs to be out by October is priced differently from one who wants a number, and pretending otherwise costs both.

steps.title: Price it against sales, not hopes
steps.body: Overpricing loses the first three weeks, which are the weeks with the most attention. Then every reduction reads as a problem. {{agent.first}} will show you the comparable closings, tell you what she thinks the property does, and be direct if the number you want is not in the data.

steps.title: Prepare only what returns money
steps.body: Declutter, depersonalise, fix the small broken things, deep clean. Beyond that, the list is short and specific to your property — and for land, preparation means a clean survey, a current well report and a mowed access, not staging.

steps.title: Spend the marketing in the first three weeks
steps.body: Photography, video, the MLS write-up, agent-to-agent outreach, targeted social, and the short list of buyers already looking for exactly this. Front-load all of it. A listing that is still getting first impressions in month three has usually already lost.

blocks.label: Home Valuation
blocks.title: Start with a number you can trust.
blocks.lede: Before any of the four steps, you need a realistic value. An automated estimate is fine as an anchor and useless as a strategy.

pages.title: What Is My Steamboat Home Worth? — Lauren Bloom
pages.desc: Free home valuation for Steamboat Springs and Routt County property from Lauren Bloom, The Group Real Estate.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: How much is your home worth?
blocks.lede: You can have the automated number in thirty seconds. It is worth exactly what it costs, which is why {{agent.first}} sends a second one behind it.

blocks.label: How I Price
blocks.title: What an algorithm cannot see.
blocks.lede: Three of {{agent.first}}'s last ten listings priced meaningfully away from their automated estimate. All three were right to.
paragraphs: Automated valuation models are built on volume, and Routt County does not have volume. Outside the Steamboat core there are submarkets that close a handful of comparable properties a year — and in South Routt, the properties are so unalike that the model is effectively guessing.

What moves a real number here: whether the well is household-use-only, whether access is recorded or neighbourly, whether the addition was permitted, what the ditch rights convey, whether the short-term rental licence transfers, and which three sales in the last eighteen months a buyer's agent will actually use as comparables.
So the estimate arrives first, and then a conversation. If the honest answer is that this is a bad year to sell your particular property, you will hear that too.

blocks.label: What You Get
blocks.title: Two numbers and a plan.
points: An instant automated estimate, in your inbox
A comparable-sales read from someone who walked them
A prep list ranked by return, not by effort
A recommended list price and a floor

blocks.title: 509 Lincoln Avenue.
blocks.lede: Downtown Steamboat, on the main street, above the shops.
paragraphs: The Group's Steamboat office is at 509 Lincoln Ave, Steamboat Springs, CO 80487. Office line {{agent.officePhone}}. {{agent.first}} is there most weekday mornings and out in the county most afternoons — if you want a sit-down, mornings are easier.

For anything in South Routt she will usually offer to meet you at the property instead. It is a better use of an hour than a conference room, and half of what matters about a parcel is only visible standing on it.
